stories.title: Indonesia’s Jakarta airport suspends flights due to ash from Mount Anak Krakatau
stories.summary: Soekarno-Hatta international airport in Jakarta suspended flights until 9.30am on Sept 6 due to volcanic ash from Mount Anak Krakatau. The suspension delayed 33 flights, including several international ones, extending an earlier halt planned until 5.30am. Authorities confirmed no imminent tsunami risk despite the ongoing eruption that began on Sept 4 and ash detected on Sept 5. Indonesia’s Soekarno-Hatta international airport suspended flight operations until 9.30am (10.30am Singapore time) on Sept 6 due to volcanic ash from the ongoing eruption of Mount Anak Krakatau, Jakarta’s main airport posted on Instagram. The suspension, extending a halt that had been scheduled until 5.30am, has affected 33 flights, including several international flights, Indonesia’s transportation ministry said. Mount Anak Krakatau has erupted since late on Sept 4, with volcanic ash detected in the airport early on Sept 5, the ministry said in a statement.
